name: Julia Michaels
notes: Conversational-lyric topline writer whose melodic habits defined a mid-2010s pop dialect. Like her writing partner she is not a programmer, but the entry gives a drum grammar with a reason attached: "the records built on her toplines use finger snaps, a single kick and very sparse hats, because the melody is speech-rhythm and needs the space; hard backbeats fight her phrasing." Those are the three deltas and they are authored literally — a `snap`-only snare stack under the quietest velocity tier table on the producer side (a hard backbeat is a velocity, and hers is not hard), `kick.densityPerBar` at a flat 1, and `hihat.continuous` false at `fillDensity` 0.06 with the roll vocabulary off. The bass follows the same logic: "the characteristic arrangement puts a rounded sub under the chorus only", which is a near-static root line at 0.90 with a low `anticipationProb`. Harmony is "minor-mode 4-bar loops with a static tonic and 7th colour", and the melodic consequence is the unusual number here: "her melodies imply harmony rather than outline it", so `chordToneBias` drops to 0.52, the lowest melody chord-tone bias in this whole section. The melody block is the documented identity: "melodies that only work as her own voice — the first time I'd written a song that sounded so much like myself that I couldn't picture anyone else singing it — realised as narrow-range, syllable-dense, back-phrased lines with audible breath and vocal fry as part of the melody." That is a two-to-three-pitch motif inside a 13-semitone register at a `densityPerBar` of up to 14, which is the densest narrow topline in the section. Her structural device is authored as the arrangement: "a pre-chorus that accelerates the syllable rate, then a chorus that slows it down." ⚠ `confidence` is medium against a medium-high rating because the research says "drum/bass claims are inferred from those records and marked", and its own [LOW-CONF] mark on the implied-harmony claim is repeated here; every drum probability, the humanize numbers and `bpm.mode` 107 (the midpoint of the stated 90—125 band) are INFERRED. ⛔ **The bass was authored `reese_sustain` and the research does not say the bass is held.** Her 808/bass line is *"n/a as a programmer; the characteristic arrangement puts a rounded sub under the chorus only"* — there is no sustained-sub claim to encode, and `reese_sustain` emits one note per chord (TASK-162), which left this model at **313 distinct basslines in 1,000 seeds** against a floor of 500. `mirror_kick` under *"finger snaps, a single kick and very sparse hats"* is the honest reading. The flat-7 is sourced: *"minor-mode 4-bar loops with a static tonic and 7th colour"*. ⚠ **INFERRED:** `followRootsProb` 0.90 and `anticipationProb` 0.18 are lane-conventional; the entry already marks its drum and bass claims as inferred from the records. ⛔ **`cellShapes` came out and the sourced 7th colour moved into `passingTones` (2026-08-17, bassline variety floor).** The list led with `["1"]`, a one-degree cell of the root that says exactly what `followRootsProb` already says; and because `bass.rs` prefers a cell over `passingTones`, a third of the seeds played every note on the root with `followRootsProb` unreadable, and none of them ever read the authored `P5`. Measured: **886 distinct basslines in 1,000 seeds**, a 0.886 share against `bass.rs`'s 0.95. ⚠ Nothing sourced was lost — `m7` is the same flat-7 the `["1", "b7"]` cell carried, now in the parameter the engine reads when no cell is present — and nothing sourced was invented: this entry gives the bass *"n/a as a programmer; the characteristic arrangement puts a rounded sub under the chorus only"* and names no figure at all, so a static root with the 7th colour off it is the whole of the claim. Rhythm, register, root lock and anticipation are untouched. ⛔ **The repair took it to 935/1,000 and the floor is 950, and no honest lever is left.** The two parameters that would buy the rest are `followRootsProb` and `anticipationProb`, and this entry supports neither: it gives the bass *"n/a as a programmer"* and its Keys line is *"minor-mode 4-bar loops with a **static tonic**"*, so a looser root lock is authoring movement the research denies; and the phrasing it does document is *back*-phrased — *"narrow-range, syllable-dense, back-phrased lines"* — which is the opposite gesture to a bass that leans early. The kick this line mirrors is two anchored hits a bar that do not move with the seed, which is *"finger snaps, a single kick and very sparse hats"* as authored. Reported unresolved rather than bought. ⛔ The bassline declares `loopVerbatim`: the entry says "n/a as a programmer; the characteristic arrangement puts a rounded sub under the chorus only", so this low end is static by description rather than thin by accident. `engine/tests/bass.rs::static_low_end` waives the saturation share for it and nothing else — the absolute floor of 500 distinct basslines still applies and this model clears it. The declaration needs the corroborating `followRootsProb` of 0.9 beside it, so the word alone could not buy the exemption.
